title: Industrial Systems Simulation
description:
Studied the principles of industrial systems simulation, focusing on modeling, analyzing, and improving manufacturing and service operations.

Key Topics Covered:

Simulation Fundamentals: Understanding simulation concepts and their applications in industrial engineering.

Discrete-Event Simulation: Modeling systems in which operations and system states change through discrete events.

Simulation Modeling: Developing models that represent processes, resources, queues, and operational activities.

Input Data Analysis: Analyzing process times and statistical distributions to represent system behavior.

Queueing and Bottleneck Analysis: Evaluating waiting times, resource constraints, and process bottlenecks.

Performance Evaluation: Measuring system performance using throughput, resource utilization, waiting time, and time in system.

Scenario Analysis: Comparing alternative operating conditions to identify opportunities for process improvement.

Knowledge Gained:

Developed an understanding of how simulation models support operational decision-making, identify system inefficiencies, and evaluate improvement alternatives.

Applied discrete-event simulation using Simio in an academic project involving a coffee roasting and packaging system to analyze bottlenecks and improve process performance.
